purpose: The iosense chrome assembled: the rail, the top bar, the mobile drawer, the menus, and the scrolling content sheet with its 16px inset. Wrap your page in it and you have the product's shell. This is the entry point of the package — reach for the individual components only when you cannot use this one.

useInstead.when: You want the iosense look around a page.
useInstead.use: IosenseShell. This is the case it exists for.

useInstead.when: You need a shell with no design-sdk or fds dependency.
useInstead.use: @faclon-labs/app-shell — a different package. This one inherits the SDK's tokens and cannot be made portable.

useInstead.when: You are embedding only the rail inside a shell you already own.
useInstead.use: AppSideNav directly, and read its guard — you then also own data-sidenav-pinned, the content offset and the scroller, none of which the rail provides.

decision: Do you want the product's chrome? -> IosenseShell.
Do you already have a shell and want one piece of ours? -> the individual component, and accept that the content-area styling will not apply.
Do you need portability off the SDK? -> the wrong package; use @faclon-labs/app-shell.

defaults.isPinned: Uncontrolled. The shell reads localStorage 'iosense:sidenav-pinned'; with nothing stored the default is width-aware — pinned at >= 1024px, collapsed below. Pass isPinned AND onPinnedChange together to drive it yourself.
defaults.preference: Uncontrolled. The shell runs its own useAppTheme, which stamps data-theme on <html>. Pass preference AND onPreferenceChange together to drive it yourself.
defaults.workspace: Defaults to <WorkspaceLabel name={profile.org} />. Override only to render a switcher or a different identity row.
defaults.actions: Empty. The top bar shows the bell and the avatar and nothing else.
defaults.navItems: [] — an empty rail. This package ships the chrome, not our content. IOSENSE_NAV is a worked example to COPY, not to import into a product that is not iosense.
defaults.logo: Unset falls through to design-sdk built-in iosense mark. SET THIS, or an unbranded install silently ships our identity.
defaults.sideNavFooter: Empty. Help is what the iosense product puts there; it is not chrome. Build rows with NavFooterRow.
defaults.children: Optional. A shell with nothing in it is a legitimate state — it is what the package looks like before a host fills it, and what a route renders while it has nothing to show.

sizing.rail: 240px pinned, 48px collapsed. A hover peek widens the inner panel over the page while the 48px footprint stays put, so the content does not move.
sizing.content: .app-main-scroll owns the whole spacing rule: padding 16px left, right and TOP, and NONE at the bottom — it is the scroll container, and a scrolling column has no bottom to pad, only a cut-off. Between direct children, 16px via `> * + *`. Page roots add nothing. Retune with --shell-content-pad / --shell-content-gap.
sizing.breakpoint: The rail becomes a drawer below the mobile breakpoint. IosenseShell mounts exactly one of them — never both, because two copies would run two copies of the open-groups state.
sizing.scrolling: The content area is the ONLY thing that scrolls. .app-main-scroll is the scroll container; the rail, the top bar and the document do not move. The scrollbar is an overlay and costs 0px of layout width (measured: offsetWidth equals clientWidth), so content never shifts sideways when a page starts or stops overflowing. The scroller is ours rather than main so the overlay bars can be a SIBLING of it — anchored to main, the thumb ran up over the sheet top edge.
sizing.scrollReset: A new page starts at the top: the shell resets scrollTop when activeId changes. Keyed on activeId and not on children, because children is a new element every render and would fight the reader for the scrollbar on any parent state change. Instant, not smooth — the page is already replaced, so animating would scroll content nobody asked to see. If your router navigates WITHOUT changing activeId the reset will not fire, and the active row and breadcrumb will be wrong too.

accessibility: The collapse control is in the top bar and carries an accessible label that follows the state ('Open sidebar' / 'Close sidebar').
Ctrl/Cmd+B toggles the rail (or the drawer, below the breakpoint). It is skipped while focus is in an input, textarea, select or contenteditable, so it never hijacks typing.
The current page's crumb carries aria-current. A crumb with no id is inert text and is NOT tabbable — that is intentional, not an oversight.
The content sheet is the scroll container. Its scrollbar is an overlay drawn on top, so it costs no layout width and the content does not shift when a page starts or stops overflowing.

propRules.rule: navItems and the items passed to buildTrail must be the SAME array.
propRules.why: buildTrail derives the breadcrumb hierarchy from it. Two different arrays is how a trail starts claiming a page sits somewhere the rail does not put it.
propRules.bad: trail={buildTrail(id, title, { items: OTHER, pageTitles })} navItems={NAV}
propRules.good: trail={buildTrail(id, title, { items: NAV, pageTitles })} navItems={NAV}

propRules.rule: activeId must be an id the rail knows, and section ids are not pages.
propRules.why: Landing on 'workflows' or 'reports' shows an empty page — sections have no content of their own. Run every incoming id through resolveSection() so a hand-typed route cannot reach one.

propRules.rule: Build trail with buildTrail(), not by hand.
propRules.why: buildTrail is what decides which crumb has NO id, and an id-less crumb is what AppTopBar draws as plain text. Hand-built trails give sections an id, which turns a crumb that should go UP into one that moves the reader SIDEWAYS into a sibling.
propRules.good: trail={buildTrail(activeId, title, { items: NAV, pageTitles: PAGE_TITLES })}

propRules.rule: isPinned and onPinnedChange are a pair. Same for preference and onPreferenceChange.
propRules.why: Passing only the value freezes the control — the shell reads your prop and its internal setter no longer reaches anything, so the toggle stops working with no error.

propRules.rule: children is the page, not another shell.
propRules.why: IosenseShell already renders <main>, the scroll frame and the sheet. Nesting a second shell (or another AppShell) mounts two scroll containers and two rails.

propRules.rule: children go in bare. No wrapper, no padding, no margin.
propRules.why: The container owns 16px on three sides and 16px between blocks. A wrapper that adds its own padding doubles it, and it doubles it only on the pages that have the wrapper — which is how a shell stops being predictable for generated content.

propRules.rule: actions takes any number of nodes, and they always sit LEFT of the bell and avatar.
propRules.why: It is a container, not two fixed buttons — icon buttons, a badge, a menu trigger, an environment marker all work. But the bell and the avatar are chrome and never move, so a user learns one spot for my account and one for what happened; a slot that could displace them would take that away.
Three things key off it: the rail active row, the breadcrumb trail, and the scroll reset. A router that navigates without changing it leaves all three stale.

propRules.rule: Everything rendered into children comes from the SDK. Do not hand-roll surfaces.
propRules.why: A div styled to look like a card is a card that will not follow the theme, will not match the next page, and will drift the moment the SDK own card changes. Cards, tables, charts, buttons, inputs, badges, empty states and modals all exist in @faclon-labs/design-sdk and @faclon-labs/fds — reach for those, and if a surface seems to be missing it is far more likely to be named something else than to be absent.

propRules.rule: LAYOUT is the one exception. Arranging SDK components is yours.
propRules.why: A grid or a flex row that positions cards is structure, not a surface — the SDK ships no layout primitive for it and inventing one here would be a second opinion about spacing. Surfaces, type, colour, elevation and interaction states come from the SDK; where the boxes sit does not.

propRules.rule: Keep invisible helpers OUT of children.
propRules.why: The 16px gap is > * + *, so an element that draws no pixels is still a sibling in that chain. An svg defs block, a portal anchor or a hidden marker pushes the first visible block down by a full gap — measured at 32px from the top while left and right stayed 16, so three sides that should have been equal were not and nothing on screen showed why.

propRules.rule: Content follows the theme because it comes from the SDK, not because it checks.
propRules.why: The shell stamps data-theme on the document root and every SDK component reads it — a Card is rgb(255,255,255) in light and rgb(31,33,35) in dark on its own. A page never needs to branch on the theme. A hand-rolled surface does not follow it at all: background #fff is white in dark mode and color #101828 is black on black.

composition.renders: design-sdk AppShell (with data-topbar='column', data-theme and data-sidenav-pinned) > AppTopBar in the topNav slot, AppSideNav in the sideNav slot, and .app-scroll-frame > .app-main-scroll around children.
requires: @faclon-labs/design-sdk/styles.css imported FIRST. It is the only definition of --spacing-* and of the SDK's component CSS. Without it the rail renders as unstyled rows and the content sheet's padding-inline resolves against an undefined custom property, which invalidates the declaration and drops the inset to 0 — silently.

@faclon-labs/iosense-shell/theme-overrides.css LAST, and after the component imports. design-sdk injects component CSS when its modules load, so a stylesheet imported above IosenseShell loses the cascade — measured: the pinned rail's 240px offset stopped applying and the content sat at x=0 under the rail.
composition.provides: The markup the content-area CSS targets. This is why assembling the pieces by hand is not equivalent.

antiPatterns.pattern: Shipping without navItems and expecting a nav.
antiPatterns.why: The rail renders nothing by default, on purpose — the package is the behaviour, not the rows.
antiPatterns.instead: Pass your own NavItem[]. See NavItems.guard.json.

antiPatterns.pattern: Mounting AppSideNav and AppTopBar into your own layout and expecting the product's look.
antiPatterns.why: theme-overrides.css styles the content area through .fds-app-shell[data-topbar='column'], [data-sidenav-pinned='true'] and .app-scroll-frame > .app-main-scroll. None of those components render any of it. The result is a shell that looks nearly right: no content inset, a native scrollbar, no rail offset.

antiPatterns.pattern: Importing theme-overrides.css at the top of the file, above the component imports.
antiPatterns.why: ES modules evaluate in source order and design-sdk injects its CSS at module load, so the SDK's rules land after yours and win.
antiPatterns.instead: Put the three stylesheet imports at the END of the import block.

antiPatterns.pattern: Skipping @faclon-labs/design-sdk/styles.css because fds's sheet is already imported.
antiPatterns.why: They are not interchangeable — the two packages share only a small fraction of their token names, and --spacing-* is design-sdk's alone.

antiPatterns.pattern: Treating isPinned as 'the rail is open'.
antiPatterns.why: There are three states. During a hover peek the rail is expanded but not pinned, so anything keyed on isPinned is wrong for the whole duration of the hover — tooltips fire on rows whose labels are plainly readable, and the organisation name stays hidden.
antiPatterns.instead: Let the rail own it. If you must know, read data-state on the rail rather than inferring from isPinned.

antiPatterns.pattern: Adding an application launcher or assistant button by forking AppTopBar.
antiPatterns.why: They are excluded on purpose: one lists applications only the host can enumerate, the other opens an assistant the package knows nothing about.
antiPatterns.instead: Pass them through the actions prop, which renders them to the left of the bell and the avatar.

antiPatterns.pattern: Adding padding-bottom to the content area so the last block is not flush.
antiPatterns.why: It is the scroll container. Padding there invents a dead band the reader scrolls through before the content ends, and the overlay scrollbar already costs no layout width.
antiPatterns.instead: Leave it. Content running to the cut-off is correct for a scrolling column.

antiPatterns.pattern: Setting display:flex with a gap on .app-main-scroll to space the blocks.
antiPatterns.why: Every child becomes a flex item with flex-shrink: 1, so a tall page is squashed to fit instead of overflowing — the one thing a scroll container must not do.
antiPatterns.instead: The shipped rule is `> * + *` with margin-block-start, which adds spacing without touching layout. Retune it with --shell-content-gap.

antiPatterns.pattern: Building page content out of raw divs with borders, radii and hand-picked colours.
antiPatterns.why: It looks right on the day it is written and wrong on every day after: it will not follow a theme switch, it will not track the SDK card when that changes, and two pages written a month apart will not match. It also defeats the reason the content container supplies its own rhythm — consistent spacing around inconsistent surfaces is not consistency.
antiPatterns.instead: Card, Table, Chart, EmptyState, Alert, Badge, Button, TextInput and the rest, from @faclon-labs/design-sdk or @faclon-labs/fds. The demo page in demo/IosenseDemo.tsx is written this way on purpose.

antiPatterns.pattern: Re-styling an SDK component from the page, to make it fit.
antiPatterns.why: Same failure with an extra step. An overridden card is a fork of the card, and it silently stops tracking the original.
antiPatterns.instead: Use the props the component offers — padding, size, validationState. If none of them fit, the component is probably the wrong one.
